content: Graph /children returns 200 items per page by default and accepts $top up to 999, with @odata.nextLink for continuation; $select, $expand, $orderby, $skipToken are supported, so server-side sort and field trimming are available. On the Kodi side, xbmcplugin.addDirectoryItems() is explicitly documented as benefiting large lists over repeated addDirectoryItem() calls and may be called more than once to add items in chunks - the correct pattern for constrained Android TV boxes. Kodi forum reports against the Google Drive addon cite high CPU/RAM from the background change-watching service and playback stopping after about a minute with the UI becoming unresponsive, i.e. the background services are the observed performance problem, not the browsing path itself. Thumbnail fetching is the other cost: every list item with a remote thumbnail URL triggers a texture download and cache write.
